trace.text: Are the supplies coming in soon friend; I need to plan the next meal.
Look. The supply manifest costs seven silver; I have not seen it yet.
Well, you must find it, friend; the pantry won't replenish itself.
Um... are the rations for the day, um... ready now?
Look. The rations cost silver; the cooking takes time.
Old Odo, enough. What else needs doing?
You alright, friend? The broth is low on stock.
Stock for the broth needs more, enough.
Odo always kept the good memories, even when the cold set in. Let's get back to chopping; the stew needs stirring.
Look. He always took the biggest portion of whatever came in.
Um... his notes were always quite precise, um...
Bram, you look pale, friend; finishing this meal is good for the strength we need.
You look pale yourself, friend; eat your share before it grows cold.
Look. Nine days left on this food, does it cost much more than we thought?
Seven days left, Bram; the pantry counts down slow.
Seven days or nine, the shelf always looks bare, friend.
Hale was always meticulous, always kept things together. Enough.
Hale always had the sharpest eye for the proper simmer.
Hale knew a good harvest when he saw one.
Enough. We gather for the proper ending of a long journey, a final meal for Old Odo.
That sounds fitting, Dee; I hope the stew is good enough for the memory.
Look. The stew will be adequate if enough meat is in it.
Are you sure you want to keep cooking, friend? The food stores need checking.
Look. The stores cost more than your concern, so I will finish this pot.
Um... is the meal prepared within, at least, nine of days?
Look. Nine days is the count; it costs whatever we can trade for right now.
So, Kit, what of the rifle, seeing as we both have nine days of food left?
Funny how the kitchen is cleaner than the rest of this scrap heap, um...
The kitchen's tidiness speaks to diligence, something you seem to overlook.
Cy, what's next after we get this cooking done, friend?
Well, the data says we have nine days of food, so perhaps a good substantial meal follows.
Bram, friend, this porridge is a bit lumpy this morning, though.
It just needs more stirring, friend, nothing more.
It needs more grit, not more steam.
Does the porridge need grit or just enough salt for it to be edible?
Bram, you always find a way to make simple porridge sound like some high-stakes siege.
